candidate.blueprint_locator: Appendix A, Basic Care and Comfort > Assistive Devices, printed p.36 / PDF p.40: assess use of assistive devices and evaluate correct use of assistive devices by the client
candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — Assistive Devices / hearing aid care
candidate.educational_objective: Perform basic hearing-aid troubleshooting by checking power/battery status and visible debris while referring persistent malfunction or new hearing symptoms for appropriate evaluation.

options.A: Check that the hearing aid is powered and that the battery is not depleted, and inspect the device for visible earwax or debris
options.B: Increase the volume to the maximum setting before checking the device
options.C: Assume the client's hearing loss has suddenly worsened and discard the hearing aid
options.D: Avoid any basic check because every hearing-aid problem requires immediate device replacement

candidate.rationale: NIDCD hearing-aid guidance recommends learning how to replace batteries and clean the device and notes that earwax can clog or damage hearing aids. These are appropriate basic checks when a device is not functioning. Therefore A is the best answer. Maximum volume can be uncomfortable or unsafe, sudden worsening should not be assumed from device failure alone, and simple battery or debris problems do not automatically require replacement. Persistent malfunction or new hearing symptoms warrant appropriate professional evaluation.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Basic hearing-aid care includes checking/replacing batteries and cleaning the device; earwax can interfere with hearing-aid function.
candidate.source_locator: Sections 'How can I adjust to my hearing aid?' and 'How can I care for my hearing aid?': practice replacing batteries; earwax/fluid may clog a hearing aid; clean as instructed; replace dead batteries immediately
candidate.source_organization: National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders (NIDCD), National Institutes of Health
candidate.stem: A client says a hearing aid has stopped working. Which initial nursing check is appropriate before arranging further device evaluation?
